verifications.note: "Double E Pipeline, LLC ('Double E') ... has commenced operations. Double E is a 135 mile FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline..." — Summit Midstream's own Nov. 18, 2021 press release announcing in-service; names the pipeline throughout.

American Oil & Gas Reporter (March 2023), discussing Double E's Red Hills Lateral expansion: "Double E Pipeline proposes to construct and operate a 20-mile lateral to provide new Permian Basin supply to its EXISTING SYSTEM" — independent, later-dated confirmation the mainline is an in-service (operating) asset, not merely proposed.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Status = operating, confirmed by (1) the operator's own Nov. 18, 2021 press release announcing commencement of operations, and (2) an independent March 2023 trade-press article describing Double E's 'existing system' in the context of a later expansion (Red Hills Lateral) — corroborates the pipeline was still an in-service asset well after the 2021 start. No discrepancy with the recorded value.

verifications.note: "Double E is a 135 mile FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline that provides natural gas transportation services from southeast New Mexico and west Texas..." — states the fuel directly, names the pipeline.

Natural Gas Intelligence (Oct. 2020): "FERC ... approved the 1.35 million Dth/d Double E Pipeline LLC project to transport Permian Basin natural gas" — independent outlet, states the same fuel, names the pipeline.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Fuel = Gas, confirmed by two independent sources (Summit Midstream's own commencement-of-service release and Natural Gas Intelligence's FERC-approval coverage), both stating natural gas explicitly for this named pipeline. No discrepancy.

verifications.note: "Double E is a 135 mile FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline that provides natural gas transportation services from southeast New Mexico and west Texas to downstream pipeline interconnections in the Waha Hub region" — an interstate, FERC-jurisdictional transportation (transmission-class, not gathering) pipeline; names it directly.

FERC Federal Register notice, Docket CP23-24-000: "Double E Pipeline, LLC (Double E) ... filed ... a prior notice request pursuant to sections 157.205, and 157.208 of the Commission's regulations under the Natural Gas Act (NGA) and Double E blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP19-495-000" — an NGA/Part 157 blanket-certificate holder is by definition an interstate NGA-jurisdictional transmission pipeline (gathering lines are outside FERC's NGA jurisdiction); independent government source, names the pipeline directly.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded PipelineType = transmission, confirmed: the operator's release describes FERC-regulated interstate gas transportation service, and FERC's own Federal Register notice confirms Double E holds an NGA Part 157 blanket certificate (Docket CP19-495-000) — the certificate class reserved for interstate transmission pipelines. No discrepancy.

verifications.note: Dateline "HOUSTON, Texas, Nov. 18, 2021 /PRNewswire/" announcing Double E "has commenced operations" — direct statement of the in-service date, names the pipeline.

Pipeline & Gas Journal (Feb. 2, 2021), quoting Summit CEO Heath Deneke: financing "further advances the Double E project toward our expected in-service date during the fourth quarter of 2021" — independent, earlier-dated (pre-completion) corroboration of the same year/quarter, names the pipeline.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded StartYear1/StartMonth1 = 2021/11, confirmed by (1) the operator's Nov. 18, 2021 commencement-of-service release (the actual in-service date, month and year exact) and (2) an independent Feb. 2021 trade-press article reporting the pre-completion 'expected in-service date during the fourth quarter of 2021' — November falls within Q4, so the two sources agree with no discrepancy.
